title: Tenant-attributed telemetry cube with sparsity-aware delta snapshots
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Console backend emits high-cardinality telemetry (route_id, model_variant, tenant, route_params) at high throughput. Current downstream tables are either overly denormalized (exploding storage) or too lossy for per-tenant cost attribution. Goal: design and ship a tenant-attributed telemetry cube that supports fast multi-dimensional rollups, low-storage retention via sparsity-aware delta snapshots, and easy joins back to console routes and billing tables.

This ticket covers schema design, ingestion path (Kafka -> Delta layer -> cube), snapshot compaction, query templates for cost attribution, and a migration strategy for backfilling 90 days of telemetry. Emphasis on predictable storage growth, correctness under late-arriving events, and keeping console dashboards responsive for ad-hoc SQL queries.
acceptance_criteria: A columnar telemetry cube schema exists with documented primary join key (tenant_id, clk, route_fingerprint) and partitioning strategy
Ingestion pipeline produces delta snapshots (daily) that are sparsity-compressed and have compaction policy implemented
Backfill completes for latest 90 days and reconciles to billing within 5% variance for top 50 tenants
Console cost attribution queries (top-n by cost, per-tenant hourly breakdown) run within SLO (p95 < 10s) on the cube
Migration plan with feature-flagged rollouts and fallback to current denorm tables is documented and tested in staging
design_decision_log: 2025-11-06 — Chose 'chronological alignment key (clk)' approach to avoid full event timestamp equality joins; clk is a bucketing of event_time to 1s for stable KV cache joins
2025-11-07 — Opted for hybrid physical layout: columnar snapshot (Delta) for frequent rollups plus small per-tenant delta files for tail events to reduce rewrite churn
2025-11-10 — Decided to use tenant_stride windowing (configurable: 1h default) so aggregation keys don’t explode with ephemeral route params
2025-11-12 — Kernel/compute decision: pre-aggregate at streaming layer for low-cardinality dims and push high-cardinality dims through the cube for ad-hoc slicing
2025-11-15 — Compression: use dictionary encoding + tombstone vector compaction to remove aged sparse rows on weekly compaction
implementation_notes: Ingestion: add 'clk' generation to console backend (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-backend/pull/3791), produce to topic 'console.telemetry.clk'.
Streaming: Flink job will perform prefix-aggregation for stable dims and emit per-tenant deltas to Bronze (S3) as parquet with tenant_id partition
Delta Layer: implement snapshot builder job (airflow DAG) which merges per-tenant deltas into the cube using atomic Delta Lake transactions
Schema: primary key = tenant_id + clk + route_fingerprint; columns: token_count, model_variant, latency_ms_histogram (compact HLL-like), error_flag, cost_estimate_usd
Compaction: weekly job collapses per-tenant deltas into the columnar snapshot and writes a tombstone manifest for removed sparse rows
Backfill: use partition pruning to parallelize backfill; expect ~48h wall time for 90 days at current ingestion rate on staging cluster
Monitoring: add integrity checks and row-count diffs to the Console analytics dashboard (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/console-analytics/pull/210)
Cost Model: initial cost_estimate_usd computed from token_count * model_unit_price by model_variant; expose override mapping for negotiated enterprise rates
testing_plan: Unit tests: clk generation logic and tenant_stride bucketing in backend
Integration: end-to-end test (producer -> stream aggregation -> snapshot builder) in staging with synthetic high-cardinality workload
Reconciliation: daily reconcile job comparing cube-derived costs vs billing export for delta < 5% on seeded tenants
Load test: run quoter queries (top-100 tenants) and assert p95 latency < 10s using performance cluster
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable clk production with new topic for 5% of traffic and build cube in staging; monitor row counts and liveness
Phase 2 (expanded): run snapshot builder in shadow mode for full traffic and run reconciliation dashboard; do not switch dashboards yet
Phase 3 (switch): flip dashboard to read from cube for non-critical views; keep denorm tables as fallback for 2 weeks
Phase 4 (full): decommission heavy denorm ETL paths after 30 days of stable metrics and finalize backfill
